interpretation: The current real-server load profile does not prove a latency reduction; handshake/process startup variance dominates these 20-sample runs. The implemented optimization targets response amplification and perceived UI latency: duplicated card content is removed from _meta.card.payload, top-level MCP content is restored in the frontend, and same-tool updates preserve mounted payloads instead of unmounting and rebuilding the shell. Browser render timing and serialized byte reduction require a dedicated host/browser trace to quantify.
changes: server response shaping retains structural card payloads without duplicating response.content
frontend card-result-normalizer reconstructs content from top-level MCP results
same-tool expanded results use an incremental update path when a payload is mounted
pure unit and source contracts cover fallback, render strategy, and response shaping
